backlogged.summary: test/assert-count.mjs counts assert calls per file, not per test as AC-3 describes. Moving an assert from one test to another in the same file, or replacing an assertion with a weaker one of the same count (for example loosening a wall-clock bound, as f3 SC-1 does from 15 s to 45 s), goes undetected. Test names given as template literals with ${} interpolation (for example F41 ES-1's loop) are compared as raw template text.

The F41 AC-2 unit test only greps stress.mjs source for the glob and '--test'. The real load behaviour is covered only by the criterion check `node test/stress.mjs 2`, which is not part of the suite or CI (the contract says so explicitly).

Several fixes widen time bounds (f21 until 10 s→60 s, gone 5 s→30 s, SC-1 timeout 60 s→180 s; f31 GIT_T 5→20, HANG_T 15→30; f37 base wait 20 s→45 s). This makes each run slower in the failure path and the suite longer overall. B208 and B177 note that suite duration is already a concern.
stress.mjs discards child stderr (child.stderr.resume()). A crash that prints only to stderr is reported only as '<test runner exited N without a failing test>', with no diagnostic text.
B177 (the f26 timing assertions) is listed in `resolves`, but the diff does not touch test/f26-verify-parallel.test.mjs. Its stability rests on the AC-2 stress check passing, not on a targeted fix.
